plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Streets and parks fill with trees dressed in clouds of lavender-blue trumpet flowers. The petals drift down and carpet the pavement in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly October to November, with some trees flowering into December
plants.location: Pretoria and Johannesburg, South Africa, and subtropical regions of Australia such as Brisbane and Grafton
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, not Africa or Australia. Its seeds sit in flat, round pods that rattle when they dry, and these pods are sometimes called 'castanets'.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Mounds of layered, shaggy or button-like blooms keep autumn gardens bright after most other flowers have faded. They stand up to cool nights and the first light frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Northern Hemisphere, peaking from October through November
plants.location: Gardens and festival displays across Japan, China, and temperate Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are honored in Japan with an autumn festival, and the flower appears on the emperor's seal. Growers can train a single plant to carry hundreds of blooms.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This evergreen shrub opens delicate, silky blossoms with golden stamens just as the weather cools. Its flowers shower the ground with petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter, commonly October through December
plants.location: Southern Japan, and gardens in the southeastern United States such as Georgia and the Carolinas
plants.funFact: Sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which is used in cooking and cosmetics.
